title: Rethinking utility-scale PV economics: Why high-density east-west systems deserve a reassessment
content:
A frequently cited analysis by Wood Mackenzie identifies single-axis trackers (SAT) as the most economical configuration for many utility-scale PV projects. This assessment is based primarily on the higher specific energy yield achieved by tracking the sun. However, in light of today’s cost structures, market dynamics and system constraints, a more nuanced evaluation is necessary.

title: New subcell current metrology for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells
content:
Fraunhofer ISE researchers developed a millisecond-scale electrical method to separately measure perovskite and silicon subcell currents in tandem solar cells using the silicon cell’s capacitive charge reservoir. The approach can be integrated into standard j–V testing without additional hardware, potentially enabling inline subcell current monitoring in mass production.

title: Italian scientists build glass-free flexible silicon PV modules via roll-to-roll
content:
Researchers have developed a glass-free flexible crystalline-silicon module architecture based on commercial IBC cells and a PET/EVA stack manufactured via roll-to-roll hot lamination. The 2 × 2 mini-module retained 96.12% of its initial efficiency after 672 hours of outdoor testing at a fixed bending radius of 150 mm.

title: Argentina’s next era
content:
Argentina’s solar sector is entering a new phase, writes pv magazine’s Luis Ini. As the country’s installed PV capacity nears 2.6 GW, demand is growing. This stems from the mining sector, projects connected to distribution grids, the upturn in self-consumption following tariff rises, and the first national tenders for large-scale battery storage. However, the market remains constrained by two structural limitations: transmission capacity and access to finance.
